Amazon.Axis declared by: three ordinary attributes in the variations property group: parentage_level, child_parent_sku_relationship, variation_theme. The theme is a token (SIZE_NAME/COLOR_NAME) that resolves to attribute names — ItemVariationTheme.attributes: < string > array, theme: string, no enum.
Amazon.Axis value stored: in the same attributes map as everything else, on the child.
Amazon.Eligibility gate: the product type carries a list of eligible themes, not attributes; the token ≠ the attribute name (SIZE → shirt_size).
Amazon.Per-family facts live on: the parent listing (parentage_level: parent); non-varying attributes must match across children.

Shopify.Axis declared by: a dedicated object: ProductOption {id, name (free text), position, values, optionValues, linkedMetafield} → ProductOptionValue {id, hasVariants, linkedMetafieldValue, swatch}; reached only through its product (productOptionsCreate(productId: ID!)).
Shopify.Axis value stored: ProductVariant.selectedOptions [{name, value, optionValue}] — a separate store from metafields; optionValues is the only non-null field on variant create.
Shopify.Eligibility gate: none unless opted in via linkedMetafield (“early access”; needs a list.metaobject_reference definition; refused while Product.category was null, accepted once set).
Shopify.Per-family facts live on: the Product (options, title, description, category); max 3 options.

Google.Axis declared by: both, required together: the typed [color] [size] [pattern] [material] [age_group] [gender] fields and variantOptions [{name, value}] (nested in ProductAttributes, not a resource).
Google.Axis value stored: written twice — once in the typed field, once inside variant_option; nothing requires the two to be equal.
Google.Eligibility gate: none: variant_option.name free text ≤250, unvalidated (qzxjvwkmp persisted); five different published lists of “standard” axes, no closed set.

eBay.Axis declared by: a child container with no id — InventoryItemGroup.variesBy.specifications[] {name, values[]} (“product aspects for which variations within an inventory item group vary, and the order in which they appear”).
eBay.Axis value stored: the same store as every other aspect: product.aspects {name: [strings]} on each member, case-sensitive.
eBay.Eligibility gate: a boolean on the category's aspect: aspectEnabledForVariations (true 73,833 / false 123,213 of 197,046).
eBay.Example:
● 
"variesBy": {"aspectsImageVariesBy": ["Color"], "specifications": [{"name": "Color", "values": ["Blue", "Red"]}, {"name": "Size", "values": ["S", "M"]}]}
(vendor doc sample, #11045 §1.5); gap pass: Number in Pack {aspectEnabledForVariations: true}

Walmart.Axis declared by: an attribute name string in an array on each member: variantAttributeNames (array of a per-type enum, minItems 1, no max) + variantGroupId (string 1..300) + isPrimaryVariant + swatchImages[].swatchVariantAttribute — on 6,957 of 6,967 types.
Walmart.Axis value stored: an ordinary slot in the same Visible.<Type> node, copied per item.
Walmart.Eligibility gate: the per-type variantAttributeNames.items.enum (2,323 distinct names; Toothpastes 9, Tires 18); 280 types name axes that are not their own attributes.
Walmart.Per-family facts live on: nothing — no group object; “shared by repetition”.

Shopee.Axis declared by: its own object in its own namespace: get_variations(category_id) → standardise_variation_list[] {variation_id, variation_name, variation_group_list[] {variation_group_id, variation_option_list[] {variation_option_id, variation_option_name}}}; 0 of 92 records carry both attribute_id and variation_id.
Shopee.Axis value stored: tier_variation / standardise_tier_variation on the item + model_list[].tier_index — separate from attribute_list; a variation option is a bare label (no value_unit).
Shopee.Eligibility gate: none on attributes (no axis flag; control: mandatory, is_oem do appear); custom axis = variation_id=0 + variation_name.
Shopee.Per-family facts live on: the item (the item itself is the family; models are the sellable units; max 2 axes).
Shopee.Example:
● 
"tier_variation": [{"name": "Color", "option_list": [{"option": "Red"}, {"option": "Blue"}]}],
"model_list": [{"model_sku": "SKU-001-RED", "original_price": 12.34, "tier_index": [0]}, …]
(batch_add_item sample, #11047 §2c — deprecated form; current is standardise_tier_variation[] with ids)

Tokopedia.Axis declared by: Era A: a global axis catalogue by id — get_variant?cat_id= → variant_details[] {variant_id, has_unit, identifier, name, is_primary, units[] {variant_unit_id, unit_values[] {variant_unit_value_id, value, hex, icon}}}. Era B: the same definition catalogue with a role flag — attributes[].type: SALES_PROPERTY | PRODUCT_PROPERTY.
Tokopedia.Axis value stored: Era B: skus[].sales_attributes[] {id, value_id, value_name, name, sku_img} — a different object from product_attributes at depth 0.
Tokopedia.Eligibility gate: the type flag (the four product-property fields — is_requried, is_customizable, requirement_conditions, is_multiple_selection — do not apply to sales attributes); custom axis name allowed (≤20 chars, id auto-generated), custom product attribute refused (12052247); max 3 sales attributes.
Tokopedia.Per-family facts live on: the product (title, description, category, brand, product_attributes, package dims).

Square.Axis declared by: first-class objects with their own ids: CatalogItemOption {name, display_name, description, show_colors, values} and CatalogItemOptionValue {item_option_id, name, description, color, ordinal}; reusable across items.
Square.Axis value stored: the variation carries only item_option_values [{item_option_id, item_option_value_id}] — a shared row by id, a separate store from custom_attribute_values.
Square.Eligibility gate: none stated; the governance vocabulary (enforce, allowed, enum, selection) fires only on custom-attribute schemas, never on options.
Square.Example:
● 
"item_option_values": [{"item_option_id": "…", "item_option_value_id": "…"}]
on CatalogItemVariation; CatalogItemOptionValue.ordinal: 6, 7, 8, 9 in the vendor's published response (#11049 §1.4)

Salesforce B2C.Axis declared by: a dedicated object: ProductVariationAttribute {ID, attributeID, displayName} — one per ObjectAttributeDefinition; values now stored on the variation attribute, not the definition (the deprecated path).
Salesforce B2C.Axis value stored: variation-attribute-value @value (NonEmptyString.256) <display-value>, position; shared: boolean switches between an inline local copy and a shared-variation-attribute reference.

Akeneo.Axis declared by: a join row: pim_catalog_variant_attribute_set_has_axes (variant_attribute_set_id, axes_id) — axes and attributes both target AttributeInterface; no Axis entity.
Akeneo.Eligibility gate: a static type list — pim_catalog_metric, pim_catalog_simpleselect, pim_catalog_boolean, pim_reference_data_simpleselect, akeneo_reference_entity — ∩ the family's attributes, minus localizable / scopable / locale-specific / unique; axes immutable once set; comparison stringifies ('%.4F %s' for metrics).
Akeneo.Per-family facts live on: FamilyVariant.variant_attribute_sets[] {level, axes, attributes} (a type-level row) and the ProductModel.

WooCommerce.Axis declared by: one boolean on the product's attribute entry: WC_Product_Attribute {id, name, options, position, visible, variation} — per (product, attribute), not per definition (pa_flavour is variation:false on product 22, true on product 10).
WooCommerce.Axis value stored: the variation post's attribute_<key> meta — a copied slug string, even for a global attribute; the parent points at the term id; the lookup table stores the id again (three representations).
WooCommerce.Eligibility gate: none: "option":"Mint" → 201, no term created, no validation against the parent's list; local attributes excluded from filtering.
WooCommerce.Example: ● s:12:"is_variation";i:0 in product 22's _product_attributes blob vs i:1 on product 10; variation 27: attribute_pa_flavour = 'mint' (#11080 §1.3, §2)

commercetools.Axis declared by: nothing — no axis object, no generated grid (axis|axes|variationTheme → 0 over 5,387 files). Nearest: AttributeDefinition.attributeConstraint ∈ {None, Unique, CombinationUnique, SameForAll} — “Use CombinationUnique for variant dimensions such as color and size”.
commercetools.Axis value stored: as an ordinary Attribute {name, value} on the variant.
commercetools.Eligibility gate: none; the vendor's own reference dataset sets color/size to None (0 CombinationUnique across 21 definitions); not checked when an attribute is removed.
commercetools.Example: ● "attributeConstraint": "None" on color and size in the vendor's sample ProductType (#11081 §5 #12); ◇ {"name": "size", "type": {"name": "enum", "values": […]}, "attributeConstraint": "CombinationUnique"} — the documented way to mark an axis

Magento.Axis declared by: one join row per (parent, attribute): catalog_product_super_attribute {product_super_attribute_id, product_id FK CASCADE, attribute_id (no FK), position; UNIQUE (product_id, attribute_id)} + catalog_product_super_attribute_label {…, store_id, use_default, value}.
Magento.Axis value stored: an ordinary EAV value — option_id integer in catalog_product_entity_int.value on the child; children linked by catalog_product_super_link (product_id, parent_id).
Magento.Eligibility gate: canUseAttribute() = SCOPE_GLOBAL && getIsVisible() && usesSource() && getIsUserDefined() — consults neither the set, the category nor apply_to; the REST route POST /V1/configurable-products/:sku/options runs neither gate (U15).
Magento.Per-family facts live on: the join row (position, label, per-store label) and the parent (type_id = configurable) — the “dimension row” shape.
